comparator.name: Archaeology
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page accounts for the full 180 EC: ten compulsory 6-EC first-year courses (60 EC); thirteen later compulsory 6-EC courses (78 EC); a 12-EC Bachelor Thesis Archaeology; and 30 EC of genuine free-choice space. It explicitly includes two field schools, archaeology of materials, scientific and digital techniques, excavation-to-publication work, heritage and disciplinary theory. The normalized target combines the English Archaeology and Dutch Archeologie offerings. The English-language trajectory is used because the normalized display name is Archaeology and the current English curriculum supplies the complete component list; the Dutch page shows the same component structure, with the thesis title translated. The genuine 30-EC choice space remains open.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target merges current English Archaeology and Dutch Archeologie offerings. Their official curriculum pages show the same academic structure and compulsory sequence. The English trajectory is used as the representative pathway because the normalized display name is Archaeology and the English page provides the complete current component list; no content from the Dutch trajectory is added.

exception.reason: The UvA programme devotes 138 specified EC to archaeological and ancient-world education before its separate 12-EC archaeology thesis, leaving 30 EC of genuine free choice. Required study spans archaeological sources and materials, prehistoric, Roman, medieval and early-modern European archaeology, environmental and scientific archaeology, digital archaeology, two credited field schools, excavation-to-publication training, field reporting, heritage and disciplinary theory. UCR has a small but valuable archaeology and heritage group—Introduction to World Archaeology, Greek Archaeology, and Heritage & Ancient Democracy—but no excavation-training sequence, archaeometric or archaeological-materials sequence, European prehistoric-to-medieval archaeology sequence, or archaeology thesis. Filling 24 UCR places mainly with history, art, cultural theory and generic methods would present neighbouring disciplines as an Archaeology bachelor. No defensible closest 24-course UCR programme can therefore be formed.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC of compulsory first-year study, 78 EC of compulsory later archaeology courses, 30 EC of open electives/minor/internship/study-abroad space and a 12-EC Bachelor Thesis Archaeology. The English trajectory represents the normalized bilingual target; the Dutch page shows the same curriculum structure. Genuine open choice is preserved without inventing electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort availability. MCCHEAM112 introduces world archaeology through material culture; MCCHEAM213 studies Greek archaeology; and MCCHEAM315 links ancient democracy, material evidence and heritage. MCCHEAM211, MCCHEAM212, MCCHEAM111, MCCHEAM312 and MCCHEAM316 contribute art, museum and heritage study, but do not replace archaeological method. GOSHIST courses provide historical analysis; GOSHIST213 includes ancient warfare but is not excavation archaeology. Environmental and data courses may support landscape or digital questions, yet no UCR sequence teaches archaeological stratigraphy, supervised excavation, finds processing, pottery/material identification, archaeometry, field reporting and an independent archaeology thesis. A 24-course archaeology-led programme cannot pass the specific course-to-concept and coherence gates.
